title: Interview with Piero Cipollone, Member of the Executive Board of the ECB, conducted by Ricardo Jesus Silva and published in Jornal de Negocios
date_evidence: 13 July 2026 (date line of the ECB interview page)
key_claim: The ECB aims for first digital euro issuance in 2029 if legislation is completed by end-2026; the ECB will recommend how high the holding ceiling can be, legislators then decide, and the ECB sets holdings up to the ceiling; simulations used limits from €500 to €3,000 and found no relevant financial stability risks within them.
frame_summary: An ECB board member presents the holding limit as a parameter to be set after the law, by recommendation then legislative decision, and presents the simulated range as safe.
verbatim_quote: We aim to be ready for first issuance in 2029, assuming the legislative process is completed by the end of 2026.
verbatim_list: These simulations applied different limits of between €500 and €3,000.
Then it will be up to the legislators to take the decision and, up to that ceiling, the ECB will decide how much digital euro citizens can hold.
within these limits we have not identified any relevant risks to financial stability
under our current timeline we will launch the pilot phase in 2027
notes: Fetched via WebFetch 12/10/2026; search returned the .sk.html variant of the same page, the .en.html variant resolves and carries the date line. Quotes manually verified by WebFetch verbatim extraction (device cannot be assumed to reach ecb.europa.eu).

title: Long-term implications of a digital euro on liquidity and funding costs in the German banking system (Discussion Paper 19/2026)
key_claim: For a €3,000 per-person limit, German banks' return on equity falls by 0.03 to 0.2 points and the aggregate liquidity coverage ratio by 4 to 7 points; the paper judges the impact contained.
frame_summary: Bundesbank researchers argue the digital euro's effect on bank profitability and liquidity is contained at a €3,000 holding limit, which they call widely discussed among regulators.
verbatim_quote: A holding limit in the range of €3,000 appears to mitigate the adverse effects on banks’ liquidity and profitability
verbatim_list: 0.2 percentage points in the most adverse scenario
declines by between 4 PP and 7 PP
impact of a D€ on profitability and liquidity is contained
notes: Sentence fragments confirmed by WebFetch verbatim extraction on 12/10/2026. Model uses Q1 2025 German regulatory data; findings are for German banks only.

title: Sterling-denominated systemic stablecoins: policy statement and draft code of practice
date_evidence: Published on 22 June 2026 (publication date line of the policy statement page)
key_claim: The Bank will not implement per-coin holding limits for individuals and businesses, citing operational challenges, and instead sets a temporary initial maximum issuance of £40 billion per systemic stablecoin.
frame_summary: The Bank of England argues that per-person holding limits are not a proportionate or workable tool and substitutes a temporary issuer-level issuance cap.
verbatim_quote: we will not implement per-coin holding limits for individuals and businesses
verbatim_list: an initial maximum issuance of £40 billion
A majority of respondents highlighted significant operational concerns with implementing holding limits.
notes: Structural anchor (112 days before scan date): the canonical primary source for the contrast between per-person and issuer-level limits. Page text is 136k characters; the quoted passages were found in the first 100k characters.

title: Europe's digital euro heads to last stage of negotiations: what Council and Parliament agree on, and where they still clash
key_claim: Parliament wants the Commission to set the overall ceiling by delegated act, informed by an ECB recommendation that co-legislators could only object to; Parliament would write a near-total prohibition on legal persons into the regulation; institutions aim for political agreement before year-end.
frame_summary: A law firm maps the Council and Parliament mandates and argues the clash over who sets the holding ceiling and over legal persons is what trilogues must resolve.
verbatim_quote: The Parliament proposes that the Commission set the overall ceiling by a delegated act, informed by an ECB recommendation, which Parliament and Council could only object to rather than amend.
verbatim_list: The Parliament would write a near-total prohibition on legal persons holding digital euro into the regulation.
Further trilogues will follow after the summer break, with the institutions aiming to reach a political agreement before the end of the year.
unveiled the 36 banks and other PSPs that will take part in its digital euro pilot starting in the second half of next year

title: Digital euro: European Parliament and EU Council compare positions on compensation model and holding limits
date_evidence: Brussels dateline 30 September 2026; Europe Daily Bulletin No. 13949 of 1 October 2026
key_claim: As of 30 September 2026 the Parliament and Council mandates differ on how holding limits are set and no compromise had been reached: Parliament's text sets a delegated act procedure, Council's has the ECB set limits within a ceiling the Council agrees.
frame_summary: Specialist EU press reports that how holding limits are set is the live point of contention between the two co-legislators.
verbatim_quote: provides for the ECB to set limits within an overall ceiling agreed by the Council
notes: Possible partial paywall; the fetched text carried the passage quoted.

title: The Digital Euro trilogues: position paper
date_evidence: 4 August 2026 (title page of the position paper)
key_claim: The industry body treats holding limits as a fundamental design feature, wants them set prudently and on evidence, and backs a zero limit for legal persons.
frame_summary: A technology-industry association argues that holding limits are central to the digital euro's design and should be calibrated on evidence, with legal persons held at zero.
verbatim_quote: Holding limits are a fundamental design feature of the Digital Euro
verbatim_list: the holding limit for legal persons should remain set at zero euro
notes: Tier 4 advocacy body; used only as directional corroboration.
